newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's annual inflation slows to 17.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Iran's annual inflation slows to 17.4 percent.

text.p: Iran's central bank governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh said inflation for the year to March 1997 had dropped to 17.4 percent, an Iranian newspaper said on Wednesday.

The Iran daily newspaper quoted the governor as saying annual consumer inflation in urban areas slowed to 17.4 percent in the year to March 20. Nourbakhsh said the inflation rate was about a third of the figure for the previous year, it added.

Steep price rises are a common complaint and the government has come under attack in the press and parliament for not doing enough to fight inflation, which Iranian officials have said is a top priority.
In December, the International Monetary Fund predicted that Iran's inflation would slow to 20 percent in the Iranian year to March 1997 from over 50 percent.
Iranian central bank figures show average annual inflation between 1989/90 and 1995/96 at 25 percent.
